# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.
I'll investigate the transaction labeling code and reproduce the misfiled payment cases from the incident.

# Transaction Labeling / Categorization Codebase Report

## Directory structure overview

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # Python 3.9.2, gunicorn :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask app package (pip install -e .)
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + bank routing pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific parsers
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Kotak.py, Axis.py, IDBI.py, ...
        │   └── (YES, UnionBank, PNB, Canara, Indusind, BOB, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Cross-bank enrichment
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF clean + string split/extract helpers
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Purpose/merchant regex library
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Per-bank regex patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # Subcategory + merchantType (savings/current)
            ├── CleanName.py            # Merchant name normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── CardPurpose.py          # Credit-card subcategory
            ├── CardCleanNames.py       # CC merchant names
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Heuristic salary tagging
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer detection
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM rollup categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # Human-readable PFM labels
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            ├── TransactionCategoryEnums.py
            └── TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**No test directory, no pytest/unittest files, no CI config.** Single git commit: `fc21c7f import codebase` (no incremental history to blame regressions).

---

## End-to-end pipeline

### API entry

| Route | Handler | Role |
|-------|---------|------|
| `POST /categorizeTransaction` | `categorizeTransaction()` | Main labeling pipeline |
| `POST /recurrentTransactions` | `recurrentTransactions()` | Recurrence clustering |
| `GET /` | `home()` | Health check |

### Standard flow per bank (Controller.py)

For every supported bank the sequence is the same:

1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)` — strip description, numeric amount/balance  
2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` — **primary category + partyName extraction from raw narration**  
3. If `accountType == "CREDIT_CARD"`:  
   - `card_clean_names()` → `card_purpose()`  
4. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` — subcategory + some category overrides + merchantType  
5. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` — global merchant name map  
6. Optional: `internal_payment()` if accountHolder present  
7. If `SAVING`: `salary_detection()`  
8. If `isPFMEnabled`: `pfm_categorization()` → `simple_description()`  
9. Return JSON records

Default unmatched category in nearly every bank script: **`"TRANSFER"`**.

---

## How raw statement text is parsed

Parsing is **not** a separate OCR/statement parser. Input is already structured JSON transactions. Enrichment is regex-driven on:

- `description` (narration)  
- `remark` (often cheque number / channel id)  
- `type` (CREDIT/DEBIT)  
- `amount`, `balanceAfterTransaction`  
- `accountType` (SAVING / CURRENT / CREDIT_CARD / OVER_DRAFT)

### Core helpers (`AppUtil.py`)

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `clean_input_df` | Input hygiene |
| `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_colon`, … | Split narration by delimiter, take slice `[n1:n2]` |
| `py_extract(description, pat, index)` | `str.extract` + null-safe group pick |
| `fuzzy_match` | fuzzywuzzy ratio for internal payments |

### Bank script pattern (typical 3–4 `np.select` passes)

1. **transactionCategory** from description/remark regex (first match wins)  
2. Seed `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName` to `""`  
3. Bank-local subcategory (salary, loan, etc.)  
4. **partyName** extraction via `sep_by_*` / `py_extract`  
5. partyName cleanup / title-case → `party2` (spaces stripped)

---

## Key file paths

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | Bank switchboard; orchestrates full pipeline |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | Bank-specific category + payee extraction |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Cross-bank subcategory (`SALARY`, `LOAN`, …), category overrides (`REFUND`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`), merchantType |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Large merchant canonicalization map |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Shared purpose/loan/travel/etc. regexes |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank-specific patterns (CHQ, ACH, ACC_VERIF, charges) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Frequency/amount clustering for salary |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` / `CardCleanNames.py` | Credit-card path only |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Display labels for categories |
| `/app/Dockerfile` | `gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` |

---

## Relevant function names

| Function | File |
|----------|------|
| `categorizeTransaction` | Controller.py |
| `categorize_HDFC_transactions`, `categorize_ICICI_transactions`, `categorize_IDBI_transactions`, `categorize_Kotak_transactions`, … | BankScripts/*.py |
| `purpose` | Purpose.py |
| `clean_names` | CleanName.py |
| `card_purpose`, `card_clean_names` | CardPurpose.py, CardCleanNames.py |
| `salary_detection`, `getmode` | SalaryDetection.py |
| `internal_payment` | InternalPayment.py |
| `pfm_categorization` | PFMCategorization.py |
| `simple_description` | SimpleDescription.py |
| `clean_input_df`, `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract`, … | AppUtil.py |
| `recurrent_transactions` | RecurrentTxns.py |

---

## Mapping SEV-1 issues → code

### 1. Cheque with only cheque number → `TRANSFER` instead of cheque

**Mechanism:** Cheque labeling almost always needs `CHQ`/`CLG`/`MICR`/`CHEQUE` in description **or** a numeric `remark`. If both are weak, default is `TRANSFER`.

Examples:

- Many banks: `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,6}$` → `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` (YES, UCO, Kotak, Axis, PNB, BOB, …)  
- **HDFC** only special-cases a 16-digit zero-padded remark for deposit; a plain 6-digit **description** becomes `TRANSFER`, then on SAVING credit even gets subcategory **`SALARY`**:

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
[transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", ...) & type.eq("CREDIT") & SAVING , "SALARY"],
```

- **ICICI** needs `CLG` in description or `remark` containing `"CHEQUE"` — pure cheque number in description alone will not match.

**Likely fix areas:** BankScripts cheque blocks + remark-vs-description fallbacks; avoid treating bare 6-digit narrations as salary.

---

### 2. `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → partyName `"NACH"` instead of employer

**Smoking gun in IDBI** (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py`):

```83:84:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py
[transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-NACH", ...) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
[transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-", ...) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
```

For `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES`, dash-split is:

`['ACH','BD','NACH','ACME INDUSTRIES']`

- indices `2:3` → **`NACH`** (bug)  
- correct employer slice is **`3:4`** → `ACME INDUSTRIES`

Also category for `^ACH` CREDIT is `AUTO_CREDIT` (line 14), so salary may still depend on `purpose()` / `salary_detection()` + partyName quality.

**HDFC** handles a related form better:

```169:170:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
"^ACH D- BD-NACH-" → sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)  # skips ACH,D,BD,NACH → name
"^ACH D- BD-"      → sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)
```

**HDFC** `^ACH C-` salary-like credits use `sep_by_dash(..., 1, 2)` (line 154).

---

### 3. `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → blank sender name

**IDBI partyName rule (same file, line 110):**

```python
[description ~ "^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}" ,
 py_extract(description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)]
```

Problems:

1. Pattern has **one** capture group → group **index should be `0`**, not `1`.  
   `py_extract(..., index=1)` returns empty → **blank partyName**.  
2. `GBHDL` + 10 digits matches `^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}`; name after space is what should be extracted.

This is a clear off-by-one on capture-group index.

---

### 4. Token confirmation / mandate charges → ordinary `TRANSFER`

Intended categories:

- `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` — penny-drop / validation (amount usually 1/-1)  
- `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` — mandate registration/verification fees  

Coverage is **bank-specific and incomplete**:

| Bank | Mandate charges pattern examples |
|------|----------------------------------|
| ICICI | `Mandate.*chgs\|NACH_CHRG` |
| Axis | `MNDTVRFCHGS`; amount=1 + `MANDATE` → verification |
| Kotak | `MANDCHAR`, `MAND VER CHR`, … |
| SBI | `ACH MANDATE CHARGE`, `E mandate` |
| HDFC | **No dedicated AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES rule**; `AMC SOFT TOKEN` folds into general `CHARGES` via `BANK_CHARGES_HDFC` |
| IDBI | only `"E mandate"` |

If narration is “token confirmation” / soft-token / mandate text **outside** these regexes, category stays **`TRANSFER`**.

`Purpose.py` only promotes to `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` when subcategory is already `LOAN` and amount is ±1 — not a general mandate path.

---

### 5. Card refunds → plain `REFUND` instead of `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` (account-type dependent)

Bank scripts assign both; **order + amount gates matter** (`np.select` = first true wins).

**HDFC:**

```20:21:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
^CRV POS|^POS REF + CREDIT + amount < 25  → REFUND
^POS.*RVSL|^CRV POS|^POS REF             → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL
```

Small POS credits become plain `REFUND`.

**ICICI:**

```22:30:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
PAYMNT RVSL|IIN/RVSL|... → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL
^[IV]PS + CREDIT + amount > 51 → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL
broad REFUND regex includes ^VPS, ^REFUND, ... → REFUND
```

Later global override in **`purpose()`** (runs for savings/current too):

```158:158:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py
description contains REFUND regex → transactionCategory = "REFUND"
```

And purpose clears subcategory when category matches `REFUND|...|VERIFICATION|...`.

**Account-type fork:**

- `CREDIT_CARD` → `card_purpose` / `card_clean_names` (no bank-style POS refund rules there)  
- SAVING/CURRENT → bank script + `purpose` can force `REFUND`  
- `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` is a bank-script category; Purpose’s generic REFUND rewrite can flatten card reversals when narration contains “refund”

---

## Recent changes / regression history

- **Git history is a single import commit** (`fc21c7f import codebase`). No prior diffs, no blame trail, no PR history in-repo.  
- Regressions cannot be attributed to a recent merge from git alone; the bugs above look like **long-standing logic errors** (wrong dash index, wrong capture index, incomplete cheque/mandate regex coverage, Purpose overriding bank categories).

---

## Tests

**There are no automated tests in this repository.**

- No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`, or unittest modules  
- No sample fixtures/CSVs committed (`.gitignore` ignores `*.csv`)

### How to run the service (only runnable surface)

```bash
# From repo root
docker build -t categorizationapp .
docker run -p 9898:9898 categorizationapp

# Or local
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# debug: python -m categorizationapp  → Flask :9898
```

### Manual API check

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "bank": "IDBI",
    "acc_type": "SAVING",
    "accountUID": "u1",
    "accountHolder": "",
    "isPFMEnabled": false,
    "transactions": [{
      "description": "ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES",
      "amount": 50000,
      "type": "CREDIT",
      "remark": "",
      "balanceAfterTransaction": 100000,
      "transactionDate": "2024-01-01"
    }]
  }'
```

Expected broken behavior today: `partyName` ≈ `"Nach"`.

Suggested regression cases for any new test suite:

| Case | Bank | description | Expected |
|------|------|-------------|----------|
| Cheque number only | HDFC/ICICI/Axis | `123456` or remark=`123456` | `CHEQUE_PAID`/`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` not `TRANSFER` |
| ACH-BD-NACH salary | IDBI | `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` | partyName contains employer, not `NACH` |
| UTR+name | IDBI | `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` | partyName = `Ravi Kumar` |
| Mandate/token | multi | mandate/token charge narrations | `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` or `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` |
| Card POS reverse | HDFC/ICICI | `POS … RVSL` / `CRV POS` | `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` (esp. savings vs CC) |

---

## Architecture summary (for incident response)

```
JSON txns
  → clean_input_df
  → BankScripts.categorize_*   # transactionCategory + partyName (PRIMARY LABELS)
  → [CC] card_clean_names + card_purpose
  → purpose                    # subcategory / category overrides / merchantType
  → clean_names                # merchant aliasing
  → internal_payment
  → salary_detection (SAVING)
  → [PFM] pfm_categorization + simple_description
  → JSON response
```

**Highest-value fix targets for this SEV-1:**

1. **`IDBI.py` line 83** — `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` for `^ACH-BD-NACH`  
2. **`IDBI.py` line 110** — `py_extract(..., index=0)` for UTR+name pattern  
3. **Cheque fallbacks** when description/remark is numeric-only (and stop HDFC 6-digit→SALARY)  
4. **Mandate/token** regex gaps (especially HDFC)  
5. **`Purpose.py` REFUND override** interaction with `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` / account type  

I can next draft concrete patches for the IDBI bugs or a minimal pytest harness around `/categorizeTransaction` if you want that.
</task_result>
</task>
